back2basics.text: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is an international treaty to combat climate change by limiting global warming. The Paris Agreement under the UNFCCC sets targets to keep temperature rise below 2°C, preferably 1.5°C, and includes obligations for developed countries to provide financial support to developing countries for mitigation and adaptation.

2026-11-10-pm-1242be2caa.deck: The 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UNFCCC is being held in Antalya, Türkiye, with India reaffirming its commitment to climate multilateralism and equity. The summit faces challenges from geopolitical conflicts and financial constraints, making global cooperation on climate action complex.

body.label: Marine resource base
body.text: India has a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of nearly 24 lakh sq. km, with a marine fisheries potential of 58.6 lakh MT supporting nearly 50 lakh fishers.

body.label: Economic contribution
body.text: The fisheries sector contributes significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation, and seafood exports valued at around ₹73,890 crore in FY 2025-26.

body.label: Island territories’ role
body.text: Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands together account for nearly 40% of India’s EEZ, providing access to rich oceanic fishing grounds and major tuna migration routes.

sections.heading: What is the significance of island fisheries in India’s Blue Economy?

body.label: Investment allocation
body.text: Under PMMSY, ₹218 crore has been allocated for Andaman & Nicobar Islands and ₹175 crore for Lakshadweep to strengthen fisheries development.

body.label: Strategic focus
body.text: The Union Budget 2025-26 emphasized sustainable harnessing of fisheries resources from the EEZ and High Seas, focusing on these island groups.

body.label: Infrastructure modernization
body.text: Investments are directed towards fish landing centres, ice plants, cold-chain networks, onboard preservation, fish aggregating devices, boat-building yards, and value-addition units.

sections.heading: How is the government promoting fisheries development in these islands?

body.label: Tuna fisheries
body.text: The government aims to double tuna production in Lakshadweep to 50,000 tonnes in five years using modern vessels and sustainable fishing methods; Andaman & Nicobar Islands have a dedicated Tuna Cluster to modernize fleets and expand cold storage.

body.label: Seaweed cultivation
body.text: Lakshadweep is notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster to develop large-scale cultivation, seed banks, hatcheries, and capacity building for applications in food, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, and bio-industrial products.

body.label: Ornamental fisheries
body.text: Lakshadweep hosts over 300 reef-associated ornamental species; the plan includes establishing rearing units, promoting conservation-based collection, and improving market access for sustainable aquarium species.

sections.heading: What are the key fisheries and economic activities targeted in the islands?

body.label: Sustainability and value creation
body.text: The strategy balances production growth with ecological safeguards, aiming to move beyond resource extraction towards value addition within island economies.

body.label: Livelihood and community benefits
body.text: The focus is on enabling fishers, local enterprises, and island communities to participate meaningfully in domestic and export value chains.

body.label: Strategic maritime presence
body.text: These islands extend India’s presence across the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal, important for accessing underutilized marine resources and enhancing maritime security.

back2basics.text: El Nino is a periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean that influences global weather patterns. It is part of the larger El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle, which also includes La Nina, a cooling phase. These cycles affect monsoons, droughts, floods, and temperature extremes worldwide, impacting agriculture, water resources, and economies.

2026-11-10-pm-3bd7b4ae61.deck: An exceptionally strong El Nino is driving global weather disruptions in 2026, raising concerns about food security and extreme weather events. UPSC aspirants should understand El Nino's climatic effects and its socio-economic consequences worldwide.

body.label: Definition and mechanism
body.text: El Nino is a warming phase of a natural climate cycle that temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather patterns worldwide.

body.label: Weather disruptions
body.text: It can increase risks of droughts and floods by disturbing normal rainfall and temperature patterns, exacerbating human-driven global warming.

sections.heading: What is El Nino and how does it affect global weather?

body.label: Temperature records
body.text: 2026 is on track to be the second-hottest year on record, with October showing remarkable global and ocean surface warmth intensified by El Nino.

body.label: Flood emergencies in Latin America
body.text: Peru declared a state of emergency due to El Nino-linked flooding affecting northern regions, with over nine million people at high risk of floods and landslides; Bolivia also declared a national emergency.

body.label: Drought and power issues in Asia
body.text: El Nino-linked drought threatens hydropower shortages in Sri Lanka, which currently meets 70% of electricity demand from renewables but expects severe drought in early 2027.

body.label: Agricultural impact in the Philippines
body.text: The Philippines allocated over $980 million for an El Nino response plan to mitigate agricultural damage, as rice production fell 18% due to drought and price shocks.

sections.heading: What are the current global impacts of the 2026 El Nino?

body.label: Crop and market effects
body.text: El Nino causes heavy rains or droughts that damage crops and infrastructure, disrupting food supply chains and pushing up prices even before harvests are complete.

body.label: Vulnerable populations
body.text: Poor households are especially affected as they spend a large share of income on food and have limited capacity to absorb price shocks, increasing food insecurity and malnutrition risks.

body.label: Compounding factors
body.text: The impacts are worsened by fuel and fertiliser price increases due to the Iran war, which raises costs for farmers and consumers globally.

sections.heading: Why does El Nino matter for food security and economies?

back2basics.text: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, is the primary legislation that protects wild animals, birds, and plants in India. It prohibits hunting and trade of endangered species listed under its schedules. The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) is an international agreement regulating trade in endangered species to ensure their survival.

2026-11-10-pm-40361fd3d1.deck: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted an illegal wildlife trafficking attempt near Guwahati, Assam, recovering two elephant tusks weighing 3.7 kg. body.label: DRI operation details

back2basics.text: Reservation is a system of affirmative action in India designed to improve the representation of historically disadvantaged groups such as Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes in education, employment, and politics. It aims to promote social equity by allocating a certain percentage of opportunities to these groups. However, reservation policies must balance social justice with meritocracy and regional demographics to ensure fairness and inclusivity.

back2basics.text: Carbon dioxide emissions primarily come from burning fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas.
